rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF JUANITA ELEANOR CHECCHI
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Accounting #1, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/19/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) Notice must have attached to it a printout of the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] (2) Notice must be given directly to a person entitled to notice, not in care of another. If a party entitled to notice is represented by an attorney, notice must also be given to the attorney, but not only to the attorney. [CRC 7.51(a) and (b)]. Did Maxine McCann direct in writing that notice be given to her only in care of her attorneys? (3) When an accounting is presented, original bank statements must be filed to verify the ending balance(s) shown in the accounting. [LRSF 14.34 D.] See CRC 7.575(b) for computer-generated printouts. (4) A supplement filed on 3/14/25 indicated that Phillip Torda is the trustee of the Survivor's Trust. Why is distribution proposed to be made to Melissa Chung? Under what authority was the trusteeship changed, and has she accepted the office of trustee? (5) Paragraph 22 of the petition claims that Petitioner (Executor) took no action without giving notice, but it appears that he sold the stock. (6) Executor and his attorneys presumably knowingly did not include in the fee base the additional property received, although the refunds do not appear to be for amounts disbursed out of the estate. What escrow? Did Decedent have an interest in real property? Please provide courtesy copies of the petition and of any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 10/5/26. [LRSF 2.7 B. and 14.7 B.] The petition was cursorily reviewed online, as no courtesy copy was provided. There could be other issues. The accounting was prepared using the mandatory Judicial Council forms for guardianships and conservatorships; a personal representative's accounting for a decedent's estate should not be prepared using these forms. Some of the schedules also appear to be out of order, such as non-cash assets. Notice of Remote Appearance is NOT required in Probate proceedings generally. Anyone may appear remotely for a regular hearing in Probate. [LRSF 14.1 C.1.a.] NB: In order for this Court to track closed matters, orders to terminate a proceeding must begin with the following language: "Order for Final Distribution." [LRSF 14.35 I.6.b.] Please make a note of it. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.

rulings.Rulings: Continued to 09/28/2026. Issues necessitating continuance: 1) Petitions for probate of lost wills must clearly state on their face that the will is lost and both the published and mailed notice must so state. A copy of the written statement of the testamentary words, or their substance, or a copy of the lost will, must be attached to the proposed order. An additional hard copy of the lost will must be provided to the clerk for a will file to be created before the hearing to admit the lost will (LRSF 14.20). 2) All notices must include language about remote appearances (LRSF 14.1.C.6). 3) Petitioner requests that bond be waived as the will waives bond. The will only waives bond for Marie Hall, who predeceased decedent, and the will's beneficiaries do not appear to have waived bond. Please clarify how the court can waive bond. Please address the above issues and deliver courtesy copies of all further filings to this examiner no later than 09/14/2026 to avoid additional continuance.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF ZACHARY EDWARD WILEY
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/19/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) No proposed order has been lodged or received by the assigned examiner. [LRSF 14.7 A. and 14.59 E.] (2) The petition caption is incomplete if the petitioner seeks IAEA authority. (3) Proof of publication has not yet been filed. (Examiner received the voice mail message requesting a continuance for this reason.) (4) Item 3d(2)(b) of the petition is probably inaccurate; if the decedent owned just $1,000 in personal property, it is not likely that annual gross income from such assets would be $200,000. (5) Item 5a(3) or (4) of the petition must be answered. (6) Who is/was the decedent's father. If he is deceased, when did he die? [LRSF 14.18 C. and D.] (7) If the father is still living, he must be included in item 8 of the petition and must receive (or waive) notice. Notice must have attached to it the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] (8) The Acknowledgement of Receipt of the Duties and Liabilities must be filed. (9) The Confidential Statement of Birth Date and Driver's License Number (Judicial Council Form DE-147S) is also required, pursuant to Probate Code Section 8404(b). Form DE-147S must be filed separately and confidentially with a cover sheet. Please provide a proposed order and courtesy copies of the petition and any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 10/5/26. A supplement to the petition, prepared on pleading paper and signed and verified by the petitioner, should suffice to provide the information missing from her petition. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.
